title: Release 2.4: carrier tracking
summary: The plan for the carrier tracking release, in nested sections: what ships, the database and API changes, and the rollout. Two decisions are open.

questions.prompt: Which night should the backfill run?

options.title: Tuesday
options.detail: The lowest write load of the week.

questions.prompt: Should the tracking page start behind a flag?

blocks.title: What ships
blocks.text: Orders get a carrier and a tracking number. The order page shows where a parcel is, and the warehouse stops typing tracking links by hand.

operations.title: Add carrier and tracking number
operations.detail: Both columns are nullable with no default, so the change is catalog-only.
operations.rollback: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN carrier, DROP COLUMN tracking_no;

operations.title: Backfill carriers from shipments
operations.detail: Runs in batches of 10k ids with a short sleep between them, so each batch holds row locks only.
operations.rollback: Nothing to undo: the columns were empty.

operations.title: Index tracking numbers
operations.code: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_tracking_no ON orders (tracking_no);
operations.detail: Concurrent, so writes continue. A failed build leaves an invalid index to drop and retry.

steps.title: Check the caller owns the order
steps.detail: A support agent passes too, through the existing `orders:read-any` scope.

steps.title: Read the cached status
steps.reason: Nothing cached for this tracking number yet.
steps.detail: The carrier APIs rate-limit by account, so one parcel must not cost one call per page view.

steps.title: Ask the carrier on a miss
steps.reason: The carrier answers within the 2 s timeout.
steps.detail: On a timeout the page shows the last known status and when it was checked.

blocks.title: Order of work
blocks.text: Deploy the columns, then the app that writes them, then run the backfill at night. The tracking page ships last.
